faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking, or through your stockbroker's platform. You will need a demat account and a trading account.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. Shares are not sold individually but in fixed groups or "lots."

faq.q: What is the difference between a Mainboard IPO and an SME IPO?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger companies and list on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE), while SME IPOs are for smaller companies and list on dedicated SME platforms of the exchanges. SME IPOs typically have higher lot sizes and minimum investment amounts.

faq.q: Can I apply for more than one lot?
faq.a: Yes, you can apply for multiple lots, but only in multiples of the specified lot size. For retail investors, the total application value cannot exceed ₹2 lakhs.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get shares in an IPO?
faq.a: If you are not allotted any shares, the money that was blocked in your bank account (under the ASBA facility) will be unblocked and available for use.
